function: Joint learned (Meta-TD3) design of BS transmit power, SIM wave-domain precoding phases, and RIS reflection phases to maximize aggregate downlink data rate (pp. 2-3).
system: BS with K=3 antennas and 3-layer SIM (25 meta-atoms/layer) serving 3 single-antenna users via a passive reflecting RIS (5x5); no direct LoS; 28 GHz (pp. 2, 4).
method: Twin delayed DDPG (TD3) actor-critic reinforcement learning with bi-level meta-learning (meta-critic) for adaptation to user mobility; offline training, online deployment (pp. 3-4).
data_channel: Custom simulator: spatially correlated SIM-to-RIS channel, ray-based RIS-to-user channel [15], CN(0,I) imperfect-CSI model, Gauss-Markov mobility; no 3GPP model, public dataset, or measurement (pp. 2, 4).
test_conditions: Gauss-Markov user mobility (1-10 m/s) in one simulator, no separate train and test scenarios; convergence curve and sweeps over layers, power, RIS size, users, QoS, CSI (pp. 4-5).
baselines: Non-learned: successive convex approximation (SCA) of [4], an upper bound, plus a no-RIS case; learned: conventional TD3 (Meta-TD3 without meta-learning); DDPG [12] only claimed (pp. 2, 4).
metrics: Aggregate data rate (bps), instantaneous reward over training episodes (convergence), and rate gain with versus without RIS, up to 20% (pp. 4-5).
complexity: Big-O complexity of the inner and outer updates of Meta-TD3 (network layers and neurons, batch sizes, epochs); no runtime or FLOPs given (p. 4).
q1_support: p. 2: "modelled relying on a ray-based model [15]" - custom spatially correlated and ray-based channels with CN(0, I) CSI estimates; no 3GPP, DeepMIMO, or measured channel is used.
q2_support: p. 4: "the Gauss-Markov mobility model (GMMM) is used" - mobility is simulated in the same environment; no train-on-A, test-on-B or fine-tuning experiment is reported, only a convergence curve and sweeps (Fig. 1, p. 5).
q3_support: p. 4: "the Meta-TD3 resource allocation scheme outperforms the conventional TD3" - conventional TD3 is Meta-TD3 without meta-learning (ablation); SCA is a non-learned upper bound (p. 4); the DDPG [12] improvement is only claimed on p. 2, not shown in Fig. 1.
q4_support: p. 4: "complexity is given by O(" - Big-O of the inner-update and outer-update phases of Meta-TD3 is stated; no runtime or FLOP count.
q5_support: p. 4: "This model captures realistic, time-varying channel dynamics" - channels and mobility come from the authors' own simulation; the paper links no code or data and uses no public channel dataset.
notes: Included, area 3 (joint power, SIM and RIS phase design). RIS present: passive reflecting RIS plus a stacked intelligent metasurface at the BS. q2 and q3 are borderline for the reviewer: the paper claims adaptation to user mobility through meta-learning (abstract, p. 1) but reports no separate test scenario; the only learned comparator in Fig. 1 is conventional TD3, which is Meta-TD3 without its meta-learning module, and the DDPG [12] improvement is claimed on p. 2 without a result.
